view.name: catalogue_menu_summary
view.sql:
SELECT p.place_id, p.place_name, COUNT(d.dish_id) AS available_dishes,
MIN(d.price) AS starting_price, AVG(d.price) AS average_price
FROM food_place p LEFT JOIN dish d ON d.place_id = p.place_id AND d.is_available = 1
WHERE p.archived_at IS NULL GROUP BY p.place_id, p.place_name

dependencies: One venue identity determines its attributes. Names alone are not keys.
area_id → area_name; area_name → area_id (UNIQUE NOT NULL)
Area name is stored once; rename one row instead of every venue.
Dish names can repeat at different venues; use a surrogate primary key.
user_id → profile; email → user_id; username → user_id
Email and username are alternate candidate keys, enforced UNIQUE NOT NULL.
Composite key permits many venues per user but only one save per pair.
Junction table resolves a many-to-many relationship without comma-separated cuisine IDs.
normalization.reasoning: A denormalized Venue(place_id, area_id, area_name) has the transitive dependency place_id → area_id → area_name. Decompose into food_place and area. Joining on area_id is lossless because area_id is a key of area; the dependencies are preserved. This explains this decomposition, not a proof that every field in the whole system is 3NF.
normalization.tradeoff: tags is a non-relational JSON presentation field; structured cuisine filtering uses the normalized junction table. Mongo embeds at most 20 dish references/feedback per content document for atomic updates; unbounded replies and votes are separate documents. Dataset checks cannot establish all semantic functional dependencies.

security.explanation: HMAC-SHA256 with PASSWORD_PEPPER, then scrypt with a per-password random salt. The environment secret is never stored in SQL or served by this API. These two hashes use a throwaway demonstration secret. Legacy hashes upgrade after successful login. Losing/changing the real pepper requires a controlled password reset.
